race_context: Center Grove Community School Corporation, based in Greenwood, serves White River Township in Johnson County, with one high school, two middle schools and six elementary schools; its 2027 budget estimates 9,617 students (fall 2026) and 1,632 employees {cg_budget27}{cg_amb}{cg_board}.

Dr. Erin Stalbaum became superintendent after Dr. William Long retired effective June 30, 2026; the board accepted Long's retirement Jan. 15, 2026 and chose Stalbaum after a search with the University Search Team and a community survey {cg_supt}.

The board has five members: Jack Russell (president), Scott Alexander (vice president), Jane Dunigan-Smith (secretary), Amy Counts and Rob Daniels {cg_board}. The ballot lists the race as At Large {in_list}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows one at-large contest, vote for 1, with eight candidates {in_list}. Dunigan-Smith's appointed term runs through December 2026, and she and Russell (elected 2010) are both on the ballot; Alexander (elected 2010) is not {cg_board}{tp_dunigan}{tp_russell}. Whether more than one seat is being filled could not be confirmed from fetched sources.

2026 is the first cycle in which Indiana school board candidates may list a party, identify as independent or run nonpartisan {cb_party}; on the Center Grove ballot three candidates are listed as Republican, four as Independent and one as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Budget: the district reports a balanced 2027 budget, no referendum fund, a 3.7% drop in certified assessed value and a tax rate of $1.1044 per $100; its debt service plan says the rate will rise to make up revenue lost to tax caps {cg_budget27}.

Budget: the 2027 plan assumes enrollment down 30 students, raises of 1.85% for teachers and 1.6% for administrators and support staff, three added classroom teachers, and new bonds for building and technology projects; the posted schedule lists a Sept. 17 public hearing and Oct. 29, 2026 adoption {cg_budget27}.

Forums: no 2026 forum or questionnaire could be read; four candidates (Russell, Dunigan-Smith, Goodpaster and Kemp) published paid campaign profiles in the Towne Post in September-October 2026 {tp_russell}{tp_dunigan}{tp_goodpaster}{tp_kemp26}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent; board president, first elected in 2010; listed on the state ballot list as Republican {cg_board}{in_list}.
background: A 1974 Center Grove High School graduate with a Purdue degree in elementary education; he later taught full time and ran a family real estate business, according to the district {cg_board}.
Elected to the board in 2010; has served in leadership roles including president in 2013, and is board president in 2026 {cg_board}.
His campaign says he has more than 35 years of education experience, served six years with the Indiana School Boards Association and completed Leadership Johnson County in 2015-16 {tp_russell}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the ballot as Republican {in_list}.
on_incumbent: As board president he said in 2026 that the community survey showed families want “a strong focus on student outcomes and a genuine community connection” in the next superintendent, and that Dr. Erin Stalbaum met those priorities {cg_supt}.
plans: His campaign says his goal is to keep Center Grove a top-tier school and continue its forward direction {tp_russell}.
endorsements_finance: His campaign ran paid content in the Towne Post in October 2026; no endorsements were listed {tp_russell}.
